9	/-!
10	# The Σ-extension of a presheaf on a slice (DAT-6, stage 2)
11	
12	A presheaf `F` on the slice `Over S` extends to a presheaf on the ambient category:
13	`F̃(T) := Σ (a : T ⟶ S), F(Over.mk a)` — an element is a structure morphism together
14	with an element of `F` at the corresponding slice object.  This is the *slice trick*
15	of the Wave-4 datum campaign (worksheet §1.2.1): for `S = Spec k'` and `F` the
16	degree-zero Picard functor, `F̃` is the big-site carrier that mathlib's 01JJ
17	local-representability engine consumes, and a representation of `F̃` descends to a
18	representation of `F` on the slice with the represented object's structure morphism
19	the Σ-component of the universal element.
20	
21	* `CategoryTheory.Over.mkCongr`: the canonical slice morphism `Over.mk a ⟶ Over.mk b`
22	  of an equality `a = b` — an honest `homMk (𝟙 T)`, no `eqToHom`; the whole transport
23	  calculus of the file is cast-free.
24	* `CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtension S F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max v w)`: the Σ-extension,
25	  with restriction by composition on the Σ-component and by the canonical slice
26	  morphism `Over.homMk g` on the fibre component.
27	* `CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtension_ext` / `sigmaExtension_snd_eq`: the transport
28	  calculus of Σ-elements along equalities of structure morphisms.
29	* `CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`: **the amalgamation seam** — a
30	  restriction of a Σ-element hits a prescribed Σ-element iff the fibre component of
31	  the source restricts to the prescribed fibre along the canonical slice morphism.
32	* `CategoryTheory.Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`: **the compatibility
33	  descent** — two Σ-elements whose restrictions along the left legs of a pair of
34	  slice morphisms agree have fibre components agreeing after slice restriction.
35	* `CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy.overSlice`: **the Σ-descent** — a
36	  representation `α` of `sigmaExtension S F` by `J` induces a representation of `F`
37	  by `Over.mk (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).1`; the slice `homEquiv` is plain application of
38	  `F.map` to the universal element's fibre component.
39	-/
40	
41	set_option autoImplicit false
42	
43	universe w v u
44	
45	namespace CategoryTheory
46	
47	open Opposite
48	
49	namespace Over
50	
51	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C}
52	
53	/-! ## The cast-free transport calculus -/
54	
55	/-- The canonical slice morphism between `Over.mk`s of equal structure morphisms: an
56	honest `homMk (𝟙 T)`, never an `eqToHom`. -/
57	def mkCongr {T : C} {a b : T ⟶ S} (h : a = b) : Over.mk a ⟶ Over.mk b :=
58	  Over.homMk (𝟙 T) (show 𝟙 T ≫ b = a by rw [Category.id_comp, h])
59	
60	@[simp]
61	lemma mkCongr_left {T : C} {a b : T ⟶ S} (h : a = b) : (mkCongr h).left = 𝟙 T :=
62	  rfl
63	
64	lemma mkCongr_rfl {T : C} (a : T ⟶ S) : mkCongr (rfl : a = a) = 𝟙 (Over.mk a) := by
65	  ext
66	  rfl
67	
68	/-- Two consecutive canonical morphisms compose to the canonical morphism of the
69	transitive equality. -/
70	lemma mkCongr_comp_mkCongr {T : C} {a b c : T ⟶ S} (h : a = b) (h' : b = c) :
71	    mkCongr h ≫ mkCongr h' = mkCongr (h.trans h') := by
72	  ext
73	  change 𝟙 T ≫ 𝟙 T = 𝟙 T
74	  rw [Category.id_comp]
75	
76	/-- Any slice morphism into an `Over.mk` factors as the canonical `mkCongr` of its
77	`Over.w` equation followed by the canonical `homMk` of its left leg. -/
78	lemma mkCongr_comp_homMk {Y : C} {c : Y ⟶ S} {X : Over S} (g : X ⟶ Over.mk c) :
79	    (mkCongr (Over.w g).symm : X ⟶ Over.mk (g.left ≫ c)) ≫
80	        (Over.homMk g.left rfl : Over.mk (g.left ≫ c) ⟶ Over.mk c) = g := by
81	  ext
82	  change 𝟙 X.left ≫ g.left = g.left
83	  rw [Category.id_comp]
84	
85	section Transport
86	
87	variable (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
88	
89	/-- Elements of a Σ-extension fibre agree once they agree after transport along an
90	equality of the structure morphisms. -/
91	lemma sigmaExtension_ext {T : C} {a b : T ⟶ S} (hab : a = b)
92	    {x : F.obj (op (Over.mk a))} {y : F.obj (op (Over.mk b))}
93	    (hxy : F.map (mkCongr hab).op y = x) :
94	    (⟨a, x⟩ : Σ c : T ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk c))) = ⟨b, y⟩ := by
95	  subst hab
96	  rw [mkCongr_rfl, op_id, F.map_id] at hxy
97	  exact congrArg (Sigma.mk a) hxy.symm
98	
99	/-- The second components of equal Σ-elements agree after transport along the equality
100	of the structure morphisms. -/
101	lemma sigmaExtension_snd_eq {T : C} {a b : T ⟶ S} (hab : a = b)
102	    {x : F.obj (op (Over.mk a))} {y : F.obj (op (Over.mk b))}
103	    (h : (⟨a, x⟩ : Σ c : T ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk c))) = ⟨b, y⟩) :
104	    F.map (mkCongr hab).op y = x := by
105	  subst hab
106	  rw [mkCongr_rfl, op_id, F.map_id]
107	  exact (eq_of_heq (Sigma.mk.inj h).2).symm
108	
109	end Transport
110	
111	variable (S) (F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
112	
113	/-! ## The Σ-extension -/
114	
115	/-- The restriction map of the Σ-extension along `g : T' ⟶ T`: composition on the
116	structure morphism, the canonical slice morphism `Over.homMk g` on the fibre
117	component. -/
118	def sigmaExtensionMap {T' T : C} (g : T' ⟶ T) :
119	    (Σ a : T ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk a))) → Σ a : T' ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk a)) :=
120	  fun x =>
121	    ⟨g ≫ x.1, F.map (Over.homMk g rfl : Over.mk (g ≫ x.1) ⟶ Over.mk x.1).op x.2⟩
122	
123	/-- **The Σ-extension** of a presheaf on the slice `Over S` to the ambient category:
124	`T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ S), F(Over.mk a)`. -/
125	def sigmaExtension : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max v w) where
126	  obj T := Σ a : T.unop ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk a))
127	  map g := TypeCat.ofHom (sigmaExtensionMap S F g.unop)
128	  map_id T := by
129	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_
130	    obtain ⟨a, ξ⟩ := x
131	    exact sigmaExtension_ext F (Category.id_comp a) rfl
132	  map_comp {T₁ T₂ T₃} g h := by
133	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun x => ?_
134	    obtain ⟨a, ξ⟩ := x
135	    change (⟨(h.unop ≫ g.unop) ≫ a,
136	        F.map (Over.homMk (h.unop ≫ g.unop) rfl :
137	          Over.mk ((h.unop ≫ g.unop) ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a).op ξ⟩
138	        : Σ c : T₃.unop ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk c)))
139	      = ⟨h.unop ≫ g.unop ≫ a,
140	          F.map (Over.homMk h.unop rfl :
141	            Over.mk (h.unop ≫ g.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk (g.unop ≫ a)).op
142	            (F.map (Over.homMk g.unop rfl :
143	              Over.mk (g.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a).op ξ)⟩
144	    refine sigmaExtension_ext F (Category.assoc h.unop g.unop a) ?_
145	    rw [← Functor.map_comp_apply, ← op_comp, ← Functor.map_comp_apply, ← op_comp]
146	    refine congrArg (fun φ : Over.mk ((h.unop ≫ g.unop) ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a =>
147	      F.map φ.op ξ) ?_
148	    ext
149	    change (𝟙 T₃.unop ≫ h.unop) ≫ g.unop = h.unop ≫ g.unop
150	    rw [Category.id_comp]
151	
152	variable {S F}
153	
154	@[simp]
155	lemma sigmaExtension_obj (T : Cᵒᵖ) :
156	    (sigmaExtension S F).obj T = Σ a : T.unop ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk a)) :=
157	  rfl
158	
159	/-- The computation rule of the Σ-extension's restriction. -/
160	lemma sigmaExtension_map_mk {T' T : C} (g : T' ⟶ T) (a : T ⟶ S)
161	    (ξ : F.obj (op (Over.mk a))) :
162	    (sigmaExtension S F).map g.op ⟨a, ξ⟩
163	      = ⟨g ≫ a, F.map (Over.homMk g rfl : Over.mk (g ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a).op ξ⟩ :=
164	  rfl
165	
166	@[simp]
167	lemma sigmaExtension_map_fst {T' T : C} (g : T' ⟶ T)
168	    (x : (sigmaExtension S F).obj (op T)) :
169	    ((sigmaExtension S F).map g.op x).1 = g ≫ x.1 :=
170	  rfl
171	
172	/-- **The amalgamation seam**: a restriction of a Σ-element hits a prescribed
173	Σ-element iff the fibre component of the source restricts to the prescribed fibre
174	component along the canonical slice morphism over the prescribed structure
175	morphism. -/
176	lemma sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff {T' T : C} (g : T' ⟶ T) {a : T ⟶ S} {b : T' ⟶ S}
177	    (w : g ≫ a = b) (s : F.obj (op (Over.mk a))) (y : F.obj (op (Over.mk b))) :
178	    (sigmaExtension S F).map g.op ⟨a, s⟩ = ⟨b, y⟩
179	      ↔ F.map (Over.homMk g (show g ≫ (Over.mk a).hom = (Over.mk b).hom from w) :
180	          Over.mk b ⟶ Over.mk a).op s = y := by
181	  subst w
182	  rw [sigmaExtension_map_mk]
183	  constructor
184	  · intro h
185	    have h2 := sigmaExtension_snd_eq F rfl h
186	    rw [mkCongr_rfl, op_id, F.map_id] at h2
187	    exact h2.symm
188	  · intro h
189	    refine sigmaExtension_ext F rfl ?_
190	    rw [mkCongr_rfl, op_id, F.map_id]
191	    exact h.symm
192	
193	/-- The Σ-extension's restriction along the left leg of a slice morphism `g : Z ⟶
194	Over.mk a`, evaluated at a Σ-element over `a`: the structure morphism is `Z.hom` and
195	the fibre component is the honest slice restriction `F.map g.op`. -/
196	lemma sigmaExtension_map_left_mk {Z : Over S} {T : C} {a : T ⟶ S}
197	    (g : Z ⟶ Over.mk a) (x : F.obj (op (Over.mk a))) :
198	    (sigmaExtension S F).map g.left.op ⟨a, x⟩
199	      = ⟨Z.hom, F.map g.op x⟩ :=
200	  (sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff g.left (Over.w g) x (F.map g.op x)).mpr
201	    (congrArg (fun φ : Z ⟶ Over.mk a => F.map φ.op x)
202	      (Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl :
203	        (Over.homMk g.left (Over.w g) : Z ⟶ Over.mk a) = g))
204	
205	/-- **The compatibility descent**: two Σ-elements whose Σ-extension restrictions along
206	the left legs of a pair of slice morphisms with common domain agree have fibre
207	components agreeing after restriction along the slice morphisms themselves. -/
208	lemma map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq {Z : Over S} {T T' : C} {a : T ⟶ S}
209	    {b : T' ⟶ S} {x : F.obj (op (Over.mk a))} {y : F.obj (op (Over.mk b))}
210	    (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk a) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk b)
211	    (h : (sigmaExtension S F).map gi.left.op ⟨a, x⟩
212	        = (sigmaExtension S F).map gj.left.op ⟨b, y⟩) :
213	    F.map gi.op x = F.map gj.op y := by
214	  have h' : (⟨Z.hom, F.map gi.op x⟩ : Σ c : Z.left ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk c)))
215	      = ⟨Z.hom, F.map gj.op y⟩ :=
216	    (sigmaExtension_map_left_mk gi x).symm.trans
217	      (h.trans (sigmaExtension_map_left_mk gj y))
218	  exact eq_of_heq (Sigma.mk.inj h').2
219	
220	end Over

222	/-! ## The Σ-descent of a representation -/
223	
224	namespace Functor.RepresentableBy
225	
226	open Over
227	
228	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {S : C} {F : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w}
229	
230	/-- **The Σ-descent of a representation** (the slice trick, output half): a
231	representation of the Σ-extension of `F` by an object `J` of the ambient category
232	induces a representation of `F` on the slice by `Over.mk` of the Σ-component of the
233	universal element; the slice `homEquiv` is plain application of `F.map` to the fibre
234	component of the universal element. -/
235	def overSlice {J : C} (α : (sigmaExtension S F).RepresentableBy J) :
236	    F.RepresentableBy (Over.mk (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).1) where
237	  homEquiv {X} :=
238	    { toFun := fun g => F.map g.op (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).2
239	      invFun := fun ξ =>
240	        Over.homMk (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)
241	          (congrArg Sigma.fst
242	            ((α.homEquiv_eq (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)).symm.trans
243	              (α.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)))
244	      left_inv := fun g => by
245	        refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
246	        change α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, F.map g.op (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).2⟩ = g.left
247	        rw [Equiv.symm_apply_eq, α.homEquiv_eq g.left]
248	        exact (sigmaExtension_map_left_mk g (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).2).symm
249	      right_inv := fun ξ => by
250	        have h : (sigmaExtension S F).map (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩).op
251	              (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J))
252	            = ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩ :=
253	          (α.homEquiv_eq (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)).symm.trans
254	            (α.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)
255	        have h2 : (⟨X.hom, F.map (Over.homMk (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)
256	              (congrArg Sigma.fst
257	                ((α.homEquiv_eq (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)).symm.trans
258	                  (α.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)))
259	                : X ⟶ Over.mk (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).1).op (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).2⟩
260	            : Σ c : X.left ⟶ S, F.obj (op (Over.mk c))) = ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩ :=
261	          (sigmaExtension_map_left_mk
262	            (Over.homMk (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)
263	              (congrArg Sigma.fst
264	                ((α.homEquiv_eq (α.homEquiv.symm ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩)).symm.trans
265	                  (α.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply ⟨X.hom, ξ⟩))))
266	            (α.homEquiv (𝟙 J)).2).symm.trans h
267	        exact eq_of_heq (Sigma.mk.inj h2).2 }
268	  homEquiv_comp {X X'} f g := by
269	    dsimp only [Equiv.coe_fn_mk]
270	    rw [op_comp, Functor.map_comp_apply]
271	
272	end Functor.RepresentableBy
273	
274	end CategoryTheory

10	/-!
11	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
12	
13	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
14	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
15	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
16	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
17	
18	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
19	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
20	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
21	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
22	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
23	-/
24	
25	set_option autoImplicit false
26	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
27	
28	universe u
29	
30	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
31	
32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
33	
34	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
35	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
36	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
37	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
38	
39	noncomputable section
40	
41	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
42	
43	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
44	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
45	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
46	def PicRankOneOpen :
47	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
48	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
49	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
50	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
51	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
52	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
53	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
54	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
55	      apply Subtype.ext
56	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
57	    rw [e]
58	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
59	
60	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
61	
62	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
63	
64	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
65	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
66	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
67	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
68	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
69	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
70	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
71	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
72	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
73	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
74	
75	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
76	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
77	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
78	contract. -/
79	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
80	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
81	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
82	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
83	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
84	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
85	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
86	  rfl
87	
88	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
89	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
90	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
91	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
92	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
93	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
94	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
95	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
96	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
97	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
98	
99	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
100	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
101	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
102	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
103	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
104	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
105	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h
106	
107	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
108	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
109	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
110	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
111	
112	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
113	
114	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
115	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
116	relative-open gate below. -/
117	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
118	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
119	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
120	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
121	
122	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
123	
124	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
125	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
126	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
127	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
128	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
129	
130	/-! ## The explicit fibre producer contract -/
131	
132	/-- A fibre of the rank-one locus over one test class, presented by an open of that test.
133	
134	The `exists_factor` field is tied to the displayed class `g` and to an arbitrary source value `v`.
135	It is the family-level content needed for relative representability; the open immersion itself
136	supplies uniqueness of the factor.  Thus this structure cannot be inhabited by an unrelated open
137	or by a fieldwise dimension statement. -/
138	structure PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
139	    {X : Scheme.{u}}

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.

## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)

Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).

Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:

- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.

- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
  as **memory**.

Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.

## Resuming after an interruption

State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:

- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)

There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
`subagents` skill):

- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

14	/-!
15	# Discharge of the rank-one divisor uniqueness interface
16	
17	`rankOneDivisorUniqueness` proves `RankOneDivisorUniqueness pi` outright: over every affine
18	test whose plus class lies in the rank-one locus, at most one widened locally certified
19	divisor class of degree `genus C` has Abel value the input class.  No auxiliary hypotheses
20	remain — the interface consumed by the canonical-divisor descent is closed.
21	
22	The proof composes the landed engines and is local-to-global twice, both times genuinely:
23	
24	* membership in `PicRankOneOpen` tested at the identity yields a presentation `P` of the
25	  input class over the test algebra itself, with an étale carrier `B := P.cover.Carrier`
26	  carrying the cocycle datum and its four rank-one certificates;
27	* both families restrict along the faithfully flat `S → B`, where their Abel values become
28	  the `PicEtAff.unit` of `P.representative` (`mapAlg_mk_eq_unit_self`), so étale
29	  separatedness (`PicEtAff.unit_injective`) matches both `relPic` classes with the datum's
30	  Čech class;
31	* near every prime of `B` the base-discrepancy localization
32	  (`exists_notMem_cechPicMap_eq_of_relPicMk_eq`) upgrades the two `relPic` equalities to
33	  on-the-nose `CechPic` equalities on a basic open — the two localizations are merged by
34	  multiplying the two good elements;
35	* on each such basic open the datum base-changes with its certificates
36	  (`RankOneFamilyCertificates.scalarExtension`), and the datum-class uniqueness core
37	  (`divFamZarAff_eq_of_picClass_eq_cechPicClass`) forces the two restricted families to
38	  agree;
39	* the good elements span the unit ideal (`exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime`), so the
40	  away-span separatedness (`DivFamZarAff.eq_of_awaySpan_eq`) closes equality over `B`, and
41	  faithfully-flat injectivity (`DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat`) closes
42	  it over the test algebra.
43	
44	The rank-one hypothesis enters irreplaceably through the certificates feeding the
45	uniqueness core's unit-extraction engine; the glue-backs cover `Spec B` and descend a
46	faithfully flat cover of `Spec S`, so neither is the trivial converse (the two traps of the
47	uniqueness-discharge memory).  As immediate consumers, the canonical rank-one divisor and
48	its accessors are re-exported with the interface hypothesis discharged
49	(`canonicalRankOneDivisor`, `existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_presentation`).
50	-/

72	/-- Equality of Čech Picard classes after base change to an away localization persists to

74	`Localization.Away a →ₐ[k] Localization.Away f` interposes, and the relative-curve
75	comparisons compose over the tower `B → B_a → B_f`. -/
76	private lemma cechPicMap_away_eq_of_mul {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
77	    (a b f : B) (hab : a * b = f) {L L' : (relCurve C B).CechPic}
78	    (h : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B (Localization.Away a)) L
79	        = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B (Localization.Away a)) L') :
80	    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B (Localization.Away f)) L
81	      = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B (Localization.Away f)) L' := by
82	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away a) (Localization.Away f) :=
83	    (DivFamZar.awayMulOfDvd (k := k) f a b hab).toRingHom.toAlgebra
84	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away a) (Localization.Away f) :=

86	      ((DivFamZar.awayMulOfDvd (k := k) f a b hab).commutes x).symm
87	  haveI : IsScalarTower B (Localization.Away a) (Localization.Away f) :=
88	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun x =>

90	  have hcomp : Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B (Localization.Away f))
91	      = (Scheme.CechPic.map
92	          (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away a) (Localization.Away f))).comp
93	        (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B (Localization.Away a))) := by
94	    rw [← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, relCurveMap_comp]

99	/-- **Per-prime local agreement with the datum**: two widened divisor families over the
100	presentation carrier whose `picClass`es agree with the datum's Čech class in the relative
101	Picard group agree on the nose after restriction to a basic open around any given prime.
102	
103	The base-discrepancy localization produces one good element per family; their product is
104	good for both, the datum base-changes with its four rank-one certificates, and the
105	datum-class uniqueness core forces the two restricted families to coincide. -/
106	theorem PicRankOneLocalPresentation.exists_notMem_mapAlgHom_eq
107	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
108	    {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
109	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
110	    {F G : DivFamZarAff C P.cover.Carrier (genus C)}
111	    (hF : relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) F.picClass
112	        = relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) P.datum.cechPicClass)
113	    (hG : relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) G.picClass
114	        = relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) P.datum.cechPicClass)
115	    (q : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier) :
116	    ∃ f : P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ q.asIdeal ∧
117	      DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
118	          (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f)) F
119	        = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
120	          (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f)) G := by
121	  classical
122	  obtain ⟨f₁, hf₁, h₁⟩ := exists_notMem_cechPicMap_eq_of_relPicMk_eq hF q
123	  obtain ⟨f₂, hf₂, h₂⟩ := exists_notMem_cechPicMap_eq_of_relPicMk_eq hG q
124	  have hmul : f₁ * f₂ ∉ q.asIdeal := fun hmem => by
125	    rcases q.isPrime.mem_or_mem hmem with h | h
126	    exacts [hf₁ h, hf₂ h]
127	  refine ⟨f₁ * f₂, hmul, ?_⟩
128	  set B' := Localization.Away (f₁ * f₂)
129	  -- both restricted families have `picClass` the base-changed datum class on the nose
130	  have h₁' := cechPicMap_away_eq_of_mul (C := C) f₁ f₂ (f₁ * f₂) rfl h₁
131	  have h₂' := cechPicMap_away_eq_of_mul (C := C) f₂ f₁ (f₁ * f₂) (mul_comm f₂ f₁) h₂
132	  have hFpic : (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
133	      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k P.cover.Carrier B') F).picClass
134	      = (P.datum.baseChange B').cechPicClass := by
135	    rw [DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg _ (fun _ => rfl), DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlg,
136	      P.datum.cechPicClass_baseChange B']
137	    exact h₁'
138	  have hGpic : (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
139	      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k P.cover.Carrier B') G).picClass
140	      = (P.datum.baseChange B').cechPicClass := by
141	    rw [DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg _ (fun _ => rfl), DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlg,
142	      P.datum.cechPicClass_baseChange B']
143	    exact h₂'
144	  -- the presentation's four certificates base-change to the basic open
145	  have cert : RankOneFamilyCertificates (P.datum.baseChange B') :=
146	    (RankOneFamilyCertificates.mk P.h1_vanishing P.h0_finite P.h0_projective
147	      P.h0_rank_one).scalarExtension B'
148	  exact BasicOpenCocycleDatum.divFamZarAff_eq_of_picClass_eq_cechPicClass
149	    (P.datum.baseChange B') cert.h1_vanishing cert.h0_finite cert.h0_projective
150	    cert.h0_rank_one _ _ hFpic hGpic
151	
152	/-- **The rank-one divisor uniqueness interface holds** (the T5 discharge): over every
153	affine test whose plus class lies in the rank-one locus, at most one widened locally
154	certified divisor class of degree `genus C` has Abel value the input class.
155	
156	Injectivity is restored on the rank-one locus precisely because the presentation's `H⁰` is
157	finite projective of stalk rank one — single-point linear systems — which feeds the
158	unit-extraction engine of the datum-class uniqueness core; away from the locus the widened
159	Abel map is genuinely non-injective (`Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective`). -/
160	theorem rankOneDivisorUniqueness : RankOneDivisorUniqueness pi := by
161	  intro S _ _ lam hlam F G hF hG
162	  classical
163	  -- a presentation of the input class, from the identity test; its plus class is `lam.1`
164	  obtain ⟨P⟩ := (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mp hlam S (𝟙 (overSpec k S))
165	  have e : ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map
166	      (𝟙 (overSpec k S)).op lam).1 = lam.1 :=
167	    picEtMap_id C lam.1
168	  -- inject along the faithfully flat étale carrier
169	  apply DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat
170	    (S := S) (S' := P.cover.Carrier)
171	  set φ0 : S →ₐ[k] P.cover.Carrier := IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S P.cover.Carrier with hφ0
172	  -- the restricted Abel values are the unit of the representative, so both restricted
173	  -- `picClass`es agree with the datum's Čech class in the relative Picard group
174	  have hofId : ((Algebra.ofId S P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k) = φ0 :=
175	    AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
176	  have hrep : PicEtAff.mk C P.cover P.representative = picEtAffineEquiv C S lam.1 := by
177	    rw [← e]
178	    exact P.represents
179	  have htarget : PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ0 (picEtAffineEquiv C S lam.1)
180	      = PicEtAff.unit C P.cover.Carrier
181	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)) := by
182	    rw [← hrep, ← hofId, PicEtAff.mapAlg_mk_eq_unit_self]
183	  have key : ∀ H : DivFamZarAff C S (genus C),
184	      abelDivAffPlus C S H = picEtAffineEquiv C S lam.1 →
185	      relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
186	          (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ0 H).picClass
187	        = relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier) P.datum.cechPicClass := by
188	    intro H hH
189	    rw [← P.datum_class]
190	    apply PicEtAff.unit_injective C P.cover.Carrier
191	    calc PicEtAff.unit C P.cover.Carrier (relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
192	          (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ0 H).picClass)
193	        = abelDivAffPlus C P.cover.Carrier (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ0 H) := rfl
194	      _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ0 (abelDivAffPlus C S H) :=
195	          (abelDivAffPlus_mapAlgHom φ0 H).symm
196	      _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ0 (picEtAffineEquiv C S lam.1) := by rw [hH]
197	      _ = PicEtAff.unit C P.cover.Carrier
198	            (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)) := htarget
199	  -- per-prime agreement, upgraded to a finite spanning family, separates over the carrier
200	  obtain ⟨m, g, hgspan, hggood⟩ := exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime
201	    (fun f => DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
202	        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f))
203	        (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ0 F)
204	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom
205	        (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f))
206	        (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ0 G))
207	    (fun q => P.exists_notMem_mapAlgHom_eq pi (key F hF) (key G hG) q)
208	  exact DivFamZarAff.eq_of_awaySpan_eq g hgspan hggood
209	
210	/-! ## Immediate consumers: the canonical rank-one divisor, unconditionally -/
211	
212	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
213	  {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
214	
215	/-- The unique Abel-correct divisor of a rank-one local presentation, with the uniqueness
216	interface discharged. -/
217	theorem existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_presentation
218	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A)))
219	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier] :
220	    ∃! F : DivFamZarAff C A (genus C),
221	      abelDivAffPlus C A F = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1 :=
222	  existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation pi
223	    (rankOneDivisorUniqueness pi) hlam P
224	
225	/-- **The canonical rank-one divisor**, with the uniqueness interface discharged. -/
226	noncomputable def canonicalRankOneDivisor
227	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A)))
228	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier] :
229	    DivFamZarAff C A (genus C) :=
230	  canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation pi (rankOneDivisorUniqueness pi) hlam P
231	
232	/-- The canonical rank-one divisor satisfies the Abel equation. -/
233	theorem canonicalRankOneDivisor_abel
234	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A)))
235	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier] :
236	    abelDivAffPlus C A (canonicalRankOneDivisor pi hlam P)
237	      = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1 :=
238	  canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation_abel pi (rankOneDivisorUniqueness pi) hlam P
239	
240	/-- Any Abel-correct widened divisor class equals the canonical rank-one divisor. -/
241	theorem canonicalRankOneDivisor_unique
242	    (hlam : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj (op (overSpec k A)))
243	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
244	    (F : DivFamZarAff C A (genus C))
245	    (hF : abelDivAffPlus C A F = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1) :
246	    F = canonicalRankOneDivisor pi hlam P :=
247	  canonicalRankOneDivisorOfPresentation_unique pi (rankOneDivisorUniqueness pi) hlam P F hF
248	
249	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyAffFace
7	
8	/-!
9	# The widened vehicle and divisor functor: carrying a widened class to a GENERAL test
10	
11	`divFamZarAff_of_forall_prime_certified_adaptation` (`…AffAssemble.lean`) is the endpoint of
12	the widened certificate lane, and what it returns is a class **at an affine test**
13	`DivFamZarAff C R n`.  Every DD-R consumer is stated against a *functor* on the whole slice
14	over `Spec k`, so between the lane's endpoint and its consumers sits the affine-opens limit —
15	the `divFamZar` vehicle of `DivisorFamilyZarVehicle.lean` — and that layer had no widened
16	counterpart.  This file supplies it, following the chart-typed template line for line.
17	
18	## The shape, and why it is unchanged by R2
19	
20	A section over a test `T` is a family of widened classes, one per affine open of `T.left`,
21	compatible under restriction.  R2 widened where the pieces live **on the curve**; it changed
22	nothing about the Zariski structure of the **base**.  So the vehicle's shape is literally the
23	old one with `DivFamZar` replaced by `DivFamZarAff` and `mapAlgHom` by the widened face of
24	`…AffFace.lean` — which is precisely why that face had to exist first.
25	
26	`[IsProper C.hom]` is carried throughout: the widened base change needs it (an arbitrary affine
27	open's overlaps are not affine by fiat), and it is a hypothesis the DD-R lane has everywhere.
28	
29	## What this file does NOT do, stated precisely
30	
31	It defines the widened vehicle and proves its affine collapse.  It does **not** define the
32	restriction `divFamZarAff.map` along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, and therefore does
33	not define the widened *functor* either.  That is the remaining item of the R2 lane
34	(`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 8 §8.3 item 2): its input is the widened form of the base-side
35	Zariski gluing keystone `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`
36	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarGlue.lean`), which should port because R2 left the base side alone —
37	but "should port" is a price, not a result, and nothing here assumes it.
38	
39	So a consumer can today be given a widened section over an **affine** test, and the general-test
40	statement is still owed.  Saying which is which is the point of this paragraph: a docstring that
41	advertises declarations a file does not contain is its own failure mode, and this tree has
42	already been bitten by it once.
43	
44	The comparison from the chart-typed side, `divFamZarToAffVehicle` below, does exist, and it goes
45	old → new only — the direction R2 asserts.  The converse is exactly what R2 says fails.
46	
47	## Main declarations
48

116	  classical

119	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)

121	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=

123	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
124	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
125	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
126	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C

130	    (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C)

137	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (admissibleAbelChartDivisor C)
138	      = (admissibleAbelChartIndex C : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
139	        - (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) := by
140	  classical
141	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
142	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
143	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
144	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
145	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
146	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
147	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
148	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
149	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
150	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C

152	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C

154	    (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C)
155	      (chi_moduleKSheaf C)).choose_spec.choose_spec.1

159	def admissibleChartValueAffTrans :

161	  chartValueAffTrans C (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C)
162	    (admissibleAbelChartIndex C) (admissibleAbelChartDivisor C)

166	/-- The concrete admissible Abel transformation in the slice over `Spec k`.  Its body directly
167	consumes the unconditional admissible divisor representation. -/
168	def admissibleAbelTrans :
169	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C :=
170	  (divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).toIso.hom ≫
171	    admissibleChartValueAffTrans C

174	/-- The ambient admissible Abel map is exactly the canonical sigma extension of the concrete
175	map in the slice over `Spec k`.  This is the comparison needed to consume the separate
176	etale-local-surjectivity theorem without adding a representability or surjectivity binder. -/
177	theorem abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_eq_sigmaExtension_admissibleAbelTrans :
178	    abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C =
179	      (CategoryTheory.Functor.RepresentableBy.yoneda
180	          (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C)).toSigmaExtension ≫
181	        Over.sigmaExtensionNat (admissibleAbelTrans C) := by
182	  rfl

186	divisor family and applies the concrete chart transformation. -/
187	@[simp]
188	theorem admissibleAbelTrans_app {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
189	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :

192	        ((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q) :=
193	  rfl

196	/-- The kernel of the concrete admissible Abel transformation is precisely relative linear
197	equivalence, including the quotient by classes pulled back from the base. -/

200	    (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q₁ = (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q₂
201	      ↔ ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
202	          (((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₁).1 U).picClass /
203	              (((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₂).1 U).picClass
204	            ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) := by
205	  unfold admissibleAbelTrans admissibleChartValueAffTrans
206	  constructor
207	  · intro h
208	    apply (chartValueAff_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase C
209	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (admissibleAbelChartIndex C)
210	        (admissibleAbelChartDivisor C) T
211	          ((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₁)
212	          ((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₂)).mp
213	    exact congrArg Subtype.val h

215	    apply Subtype.ext
216	    exact (chartValueAff_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase C
217	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C) (admissibleAbelChartIndex C)
218	        (admissibleAbelChartDivisor C) T
219	          ((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₁)
220	          ((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₂)).mpr h
221	
222	variable (C) in
223	/-- Evaluation of the ambient admissible Sigma chart on the left leg of a slice point is the
224	same slice Abel value, transported to the point's actual structure morphism. -/
225	theorem abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left
226	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
227	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C) :
228	    (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C).app (op T.left) q.left =
229	      (⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q⟩ :
230	        (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T.left)) := by
231	  rw [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_eq_sigmaExtension_admissibleAbelTrans]
232	  change (⟨q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom, _⟩ :
233	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T.left)) =
234	    ⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q⟩
235	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) q.w ?_
236	  let e : Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom) ⟶ T :=
237	    Over.mkCongr q.w
238	  let q' : Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom) ⟶
239	      divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C :=
240	    Over.homMk q.left rfl
241	  have hq : e ≫ q = q' := by
242	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
243	    exact Category.id_comp _
244	  change (pic0TypeFunctor C).map e.op
245	      ((admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q) =
246	    (admissibleAbelTrans C).app
247	      (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C).hom))) q'
248	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
249	    ((admissibleAbelTrans C).naturality e.op) q
250	  have hmap : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C)).map e.op q = q' := by
251	    exact hq
252	  simpa only [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, hmap] using hnat.symm

255	/-- The kernel of the actual ambient admissible Abel chart on points over a fixed test scheme is
256	exactly relative linear equivalence, including the quotient by classes pulled back from the
257	base. -/
258	theorem abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase
259	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}

261	    (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C).app (op T.left) q₁.left =
262	        (abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible C).app (op T.left) q₂.left
263	      ↔ ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
264	          (((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₁).1 U).picClass /
265	              (((divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy C).homEquiv q₂).1 U).picClass
266	            ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) := by
267	  rw [abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left C q₁,
268	    abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_app_left C q₂]
269	  change (⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q₁⟩ :
270	      (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T.left)) =
271	        ⟨T.hom, (admissibleAbelTrans C).app (op T) q₂⟩ ↔ _

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneSectionFibreNonzero
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorDatumSectionOfClass
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyMonoH1
9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafFibre

11	/-!
12	# T5 core — uniqueness of the divisor family in a rank-one datum class
13	
14	The localization-free heart of the `RankOneDivisorUniqueness` discharge: over an arbitrary
15	test algebra `B` carrying a pinned cocycle datum whose `H⁰` is finite, projective, and of
16	stalk rank one, **at most one** widened locally certified divisor family of degree
17	`genus C` has Picard class the datum's Čech class
18	(`divFamZarAff_eq_of_picClass_eq_cechPicClass`).
19	
20	The proof is the assembly of the three landed engines, with no localization anywhere:
21	
22	* T3 (`exists_gluedSection_sectionLocalEquations_divEq`) cuts each family, up to `DivEq`,
23	  from a germ-regular global section of the datum's glued sheaf;
24	* T4 (`tmul_residueField_ne_zero_of_divEq_certified`) makes the two `H⁰` classes
25	  fibrewise-nonzero at every prime of the base;
26	* the rank-one unit-extraction engine
27	  (`Module.existsUnique_unit_smul_of_forall_tmul_ne_zero`) then exhibits the second `H⁰`
28	  class as a global unit multiple of the first, and the unit-rescaling law
29	  (`sectionLocalEquations_smul_divEq`) transports the cut divisors into each other.
30	
31	The `DivEq` chain `d₁ ∼ cut(s₁) ∼ cut(v·s₁) = cut(s₂) ∼ d₂` closes equality in the
32	`DivFamZarAff` quotient (`mk_eq_mk_iff`).
33	
34	This is the exact reason injectivity is restored on the rank-one locus — single-point
35	linear systems — as demanded by the uniqueness-discharge memory (I-1981, trap 2): the
36	rank-one hypotheses enter irreplaceably through the unit-extraction engine, and nothing
37	here restates the uniqueness goal as a hypothesis.  The remaining (localizing) work of the
38	discharge — matching each family's class to a presentation datum near every prime — is the
39	per-prime base-discrepancy assembly, not this file.
40	-/
41	
42	set_option autoImplicit false
43	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
44	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
45	
46	universe u
47	
48	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
49	open scoped TensorProduct
50	
51	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
52	
53	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
54	
55	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
56	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
57	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
58	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
59	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k}
60	
61	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
62	
63	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
64	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
65	/-- Equal glued sections cut equal local-equation systems (the germ-regularity witnesses
66	are proof-irrelevant). -/
67	private lemma sectionLocalEquations_congr [IsAffineHom pi]
68	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
69	    {s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)} (hss' : s = s')
70	    (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
71	    (hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ x))
72	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (x : relCurve C B) (hx : x ∈ D.pieces j),
73	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) x hx).hom (D.component s j)
74	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk x))
75	    (hreg' : ∀ (j : D.index) (x : relCurve C B) (hx : x ∈ D.pieces j),
76	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) x hx).hom (D.component s' j)
77	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk x)) :
78	    D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg = D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲 σ hσ hreg' := by
79	  cases hss'
80	  rfl
81	
82	/-- **Uniqueness of the divisor family in a rank-one datum class** (the T5 core, with no
83	localization): over an arbitrary test algebra whose pinned cocycle datum has `H⁰` finite,
84	projective, and of stalk rank one at every prime, two widened locally certified divisor
85	families of degree `genus C` with Picard class the datum's Čech class are equal.
86	
87	The two families are cut from `H⁰` classes of the datum (T3); both classes are
88	fibrewise-nonzero at every prime (T4), so the rank-one engine makes the second a global
89	unit multiple of the first, and unit rescaling does not move the cut divisor. -/
90	theorem divFamZarAff_eq_of_picClass_eq_cechPicClass [IsFinite pi]
91	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
92	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 1))
93	    (hfin : Module.Finite B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0))
94	    (hproj : Module.Projective B (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0))
95	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
96	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) p = 1)
97	    (F₁ F₂ : DivFamZarAff C B (genus C))
98	    (h₁ : F₁.picClass = D.cechPicClass)
99	    (h₂ : F₂.picClass = D.cechPicClass) :
100	    F₁ = F₂ := by
101	  classical
102	  haveI := hfin
103	  haveI := hproj
104	  induction F₁ using Quotient.ind with | _ x₁ => ?_
105	  induction F₂ using Quotient.ind with | _ x₂ => ?_
106	  obtain ⟨d₁, hd₁⟩ := x₁
107	  obtain ⟨d₂, hd₂⟩ := x₂
108	  have h₁' : d₁.picClass = D.cechPicClass := h₁
109	  have h₂' : d₂.picClass = D.cechPicClass := h₂
110	  -- T3: cut both families from glued sections
111	  obtain ⟨s₁, hreg₁, hdiv₁⟩ := D.exists_gluedSection_sectionLocalEquations_divEq d₁ h₁'
112	  obtain ⟨s₂, hreg₂, hdiv₂⟩ := D.exists_gluedSection_sectionLocalEquations_divEq d₂ h₂'
113	  -- realize the sections as `H⁰` classes
114	  obtain ⟨y₁, rfl⟩ : ∃ y, Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
115	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
116	      isTerminalTop D.sheaf y = s₁ :=
117	    ⟨(Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ _ isTerminalTop D.sheaf).symm s₁,
118	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ _ isTerminalTop D.sheaf).apply_symm_apply s₁⟩
119	  obtain ⟨y₂, rfl⟩ : ∃ y, Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
120	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
121	      isTerminalTop D.sheaf y = s₂ :=
122	    ⟨(Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ _ isTerminalTop D.sheaf).symm s₂,
123	      (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ _ isTerminalTop D.sheaf).apply_symm_apply s₂⟩
124	  set e₀ := Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
125	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
126	    isTerminalTop D.sheaf with he₀
127	  -- T4: both `H⁰` classes are fibrewise-nonzero at every prime
128	  have hH1' : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1 :=
129	    (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff D).mpr hH1
130	  have hq₁ : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
131	      (y₁ ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
132	        Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 :=
133	    fun p => D.tmul_residueField_ne_zero_of_divEq_certified hH1' y₁
134	      D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg₁ hd₁
135	      (hdiv₁ D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex fun _ => le_rfl) p
136	  have hq₂ : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
137	      (y₂ ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
138	        Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 :=
139	    fun p => D.tmul_residueField_ne_zero_of_divEq_certified hH1' y₂
140	      D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg₂ hd₂
141	      (hdiv₂ D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex fun _ => le_rfl) p
142	  -- the rank-one engine: the second class is a global unit multiple of the first
143	  obtain ⟨v, hv, -⟩ := Module.existsUnique_unit_smul_of_forall_tmul_ne_zero
144	    (B := B) (Q := Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0) hrank y₁ y₂ hq₁ hq₂
145	  -- transport the unit through the sections and chain the divisor equalities
146	  have hs₂ : e₀ y₂ = (v : B) • e₀ y₁ := by rw [hv, map_smul]
147	  have hreg_smul : ∀ (j : D.index) (x : relCurve C B) (hx : x ∈ D.pieces j),
148	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) x hx).hom
149	        (D.component ((v : B) • e₀ y₁) j)
150	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk x) :=
151	    D.germ_component_smul_mem_nonZeroDivisors v (e₀ y₁) hreg₁
152	  have hcongr : D.sectionLocalEquations (e₀ y₂) D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
153	        (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg₂
154	      = D.sectionLocalEquations ((v : B) • e₀ y₁) D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
155	        (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg_smul :=
156	    D.sectionLocalEquations_congr hs₂ D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
157	      hreg₂ hreg_smul
158	  have hchain₁ : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁
159	      (D.sectionLocalEquations (e₀ y₁) D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
160	        (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg₁) :=
161	    (hdiv₁ D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex fun _ => le_rfl).symm
162	  have hchain₂ : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq
163	      (D.sectionLocalEquations (e₀ y₁) D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
164	        (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg₁)
165	      (D.sectionLocalEquations ((v : B) • e₀ y₁) D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
166	        (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg_smul) :=
167	    (D.sectionLocalEquations_smul_divEq v (e₀ y₁) D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
168	      (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg₁ hreg_smul).symm
169	  have hchain₃ : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq
170	      (D.sectionLocalEquations ((v : B) • e₀ y₁) D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex
171	        (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg_smul) d₂ :=
172	    hcongr ▸ hdiv₂ D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex fun _ => le_rfl
173	  exact DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr (hchain₁.trans (hchain₂.trans hchain₃))
174	
175	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

8	/-!
9	# Functoriality of the WIDENED vehicle along an arbitrary test morphism (R2, residue (b))
10	
11	The widened vehicle `divFamZarAff` (`…AffVehicle.lean`) is functorial along an **arbitrary**
12	morphism `f : T' ⟶ T` of test objects: the value of the restricted family at an affine open
13	`W ⊆ T'.left` — whose `f`-image need not lie in any affine open of `T.left` — is *glued* over a
14	finite basic-open refinement of `W` subordinate to the preimages of affine opens, using the
15	widened S5b Zariski keystones through the basic-open toolkit (`…AffMapKit.lean`).
16	
17	This is the last packaging layer of R2 residue (b): with it the widened carrier of protection
18	I-0492 is a functor on the whole slice over `Spec k`, which is the generality every DD-R
19	consumer (`DivRepGlobalData.pull_comp`) is stated at.
20	
21	## Main declarations
22	
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff.IsPullbackValue` — the characterizing property of the glued
24	  value, with `pullbackValue_unique` (Zariski separation) and `exists_isPullbackValue`
25	  (Zariski gluing).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff.map C n f : divFamZarAff C n T → divFamZarAff C n T'`, with
27	  `map_id`, `map_comp`, and the no-gluing evaluation `mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom`.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_naturality` — over affine tests, `map` along
29	  `Spec` of an algebra map is `DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom` of that map under the widened affine

`DivFamZar` — the class map `DivFamZarAff.picClass` is all that is consumed, and it never saw
the cover, so no chart typing enters. -/
def abelDivAffPlus (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (F₀ : DivFamZarAff C A n) :
    PicEtAff C A :=
  PicEtAff.unit C A (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) F₀.picClass)

/-- **Naturality of the widened affine Abel transformation in the test algebra**
(`DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlg` + `PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit`): base change of the widened Abel
value is the Abel value of the base-changed class. -/
theorem abelDivAffPlus_mapAlgHom {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra k B] (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (F₀ : DivFamZarAff C A n) :
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (abelDivAffPlus C A F₀)
      = abelDivAffPlus C B (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ F₀) := by
  letI : Algebra A B := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower k A B := .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (φ.commutes a).symm
  have hclass : (DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom φ F₀).picClass
      = Scheme.CechPic.map (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left F₀.picClass := by
    have hcurve : relCurveMap C A B = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left := by
      refine congrArg (fun ψ : overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k A => (C ◁ ψ).left) ?_
      exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
    rw [← hcurve]
    exact DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlg B n F₀
  calc PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ (abelDivAffPlus C A F₀)
      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicAlgMap C φ
          (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) F₀.picClass)) := PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit C φ _
